summary: Contestants demonstrate their knowledge and skills in Java programming by completing tasks that involve structured design, algorithm development, and object-oriented methodologies. The event is completed on a Windows computer using an approved IDE, and includes an optional certification test at the national level. All work is done on-site and submitted electronically.
time_limits: No more than ten (10) minutes orientation
No more than ninety (90) minutes testing time
No more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
No more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test
submission_requirements: All student-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Computer or laptop/notebook (USB-Type A or adapter required); a full-size keyboard may be used (no printer is needed) and supporting equipment (extension cords, etc.)
Contestant must use one of these IDEs: IntelliJ, Eclipse, NetBeans, BlueJ, VSCode
Only pre-written code that is hard copied is allowed
competencies: Demonstrate proficiency in Java programming and apply algorithmic thinking and language syntax, core concepts, and modern practices to implement effective Java solutions
Develop modular, maintainable programs using foundational object-oriented principles
Use Java file I/O to read, write, and manage data in applications
Apply structured and object-oriented design techniques and implement effective error handling strategies to create scalable, maintainable, and resilient Java applications
Create and interpret UML diagrams to model software architecture and communicate design decisions in Java projects
Utilize the Java Collections Framework to efficiently store, manage, and manipulate data using lists, sets, maps, iterators, or collection algorithms
Apply standard Java libraries and modern language features to write clean, maintainable code
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
Business Professionals of America assumes no responsibility for hardware/software provided by the contestant
No equipment, supplies or materials other than those specified for the event will be allowed in the testing area
Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification
Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event.
